title: Automatic Functional Characterization of Chains of Thought Generated by Reasoning Models
content: Reasoning models generate chains of thought (gCoT) that externalize deliberations, calculations, verifications, corrections and alternatives, and are today a principal source of information about their behavior. The literature examines their faithfulness to internal computation, answer correctness, length and step quality, or describes their structure with step-level graphs and trees; multi-step operations and their relations remain less characterized. This work proposes describing that organization through a functional profile obtained with an automatic, language-model-supported method that represents each chain as a graph, identifies its episodes and summarizes their relations. Validity and reliability were tested: on a control corpus the method detected all explicit deliberative episodes and 71% of implicit ones; on real chains, group means of 25 chains proved reliable. In 200 chains from four models on shared medical and legal problems, organization differed between models and was similar across domains; verifications rarely refuted (8%) and alternatives were rarely adopted (2%). The results suggest that the profile captures each model’s features: it allowed the generating model to be identified in 67% of chains, versus 49% with correctness, length and domain, and added no detectable information about correctness. Profiles describe the observable chain organization at the group level, not the models’ internal process.
